scope: Internal artifact-v1 raw-byte RPC transport, durable registry retention before WAL adoption, and bounded binary frame codec

priorSupplementalValidation.note: Passed before artifact binary-frame codec was introduced; not counted in current204 checks

observations: Actual mutual-TLS gRPC transfer spans multiple 64 KiB chunks, with independent source and receiver roots
Durable retained artifact and WAL snapshot exist before restore callback executes
Retention returning false prevents WAL snapshot persistence; full transfer retry succeeds
Failed restore leaves durable pending snapshot and retained bytes; member restart resolves reference from file WAL after scratch cleanup
Reject missing callbacks, metadata/digest mismatch, oversized headers, corrupt raw data and reference-only legacy transfers
Binary codec preserves arbitrary byte values, rejects malformed/truncated lengths and limits each of three frame sections to 64 KiB

heapProbe.transport: Two real loopback gRPC members in one SBCL process; receiver has a real file WAL; restore callback records reference, followed by explicit application materialization/reload

resolvedFailure.afterBinaryCodec: Same payload and heap pass using raw octet sections

limitations: Production start-ha-control-plane restore callbacks and outer ingress/writer barriers remain unwired
No automatic application compaction or artifact GC enabled
No native multi-process or constrained-heap TLS acceptance in this change
Artifact support requires updated receiver and configured callbacks; no capability negotiation
Per-record validation bounds and identity-index growth remain as documented
